chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), that he said:
In a bequest of his to one of his sons, or he said: My father said to one of his sons: Beware of joking, for it removes the light of your faith and lightens your manliness.

key_terms.الْمِزَاح: Joking, playful banter, or lighthearted humor

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social consequence of excessive joking in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (or his father Imam al-Kazim, depending on the chain's specific attribution in scholarly commentary) warns against excessive jesting (al-mizah), noting that it erodes the 'light of faith' (nur al-iman) and diminishes personal dignity (muru'ah). This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing joy with solemnity, ensuring that humor does not lead to frivolity or the neglect of spiritual presence. The concept of muru'ah here extends beyond mere masculinity to encompass moral integrity and gravitas in social interactions.
